You’re right that money drives a lot of these outcomes — subsidies and profit motives keep industries tied to old models. As someone who works in healthcare, I’ll say plainly: most clinicians want people healthy, so the “keep people sick” line is too conspiratorial. That said, perverse incentives do exist — high drug prices, fee-for-service care, regulatory capture, and crony subsidies for fossil fuels. The solution isn’t hand-wringing but fixing incentives: more transparency, competition, ending wasteful subsidies, holding big players accountable, and pushing policies that align profit with the public good. That’s how we make economic incentives work for everyone, not against us.
